newsitem.title: CHINA: China province says will complement Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: China province says will complement Hong Kong.

text.p: The economy of China's southern Guangdong province will play an increasingly complementary role to Hong Kong's after the British colony returns to Beijing rule on July 1, Guangdong's governor said on Thursday.
"The Hong Kong and Guangdong economies have always supplemented each other," Lu Ruihua told a news conference in Beijing. "They will be increasingly complementary."
While Hong Kong has highly developed trade links and information systems, Guangdong has a huge market and a booming economy, Lu said.
Hong Kong's ongoing economic restructuring would give a further boost to its Chinese neighbour, he said.
Lu gave no details of how Guangdong would benefit or how the ending of more than 150 years of colonial rule in Hong Kong was expected to affect the provincial economy this year.
Many economists have said the return of Hong Kong would spur spending on roads and ports linking the two areas.
Guangdong's gross domestic product had grown 11 percent in 1996, and a 10 percent rise was expected this year, Lu said.
He said he fully backed the 8.0 percent growth rate set for the China by Premier Li Peng this month, but said Guangdong could afford to go faster than the national economy as a whole.
